svg.aria-label: The aircraft inspection image is really two different images. On the left, the airframe exterior image: a large, mostly smooth painted surface captured by a drone, a ground robot or a fixed hangar gantry, where defects such as dents, lightning-strike marks, paint loss, cracks, corrosion and missing fasteners are small against a huge field, and every finding must be mapped to a position on the aircraft. On the right, the engine borescope image: a close-up through a snake camera inside the engine, of rotating blades that look almost identical, under a point light with metallic glare, where the defects are nicks, dents, cracks, burns, coating loss and tip curl. Both feed the same output: a disposition (serviceable, monitor, repair, remove) checked against manual limits, with a signed human release. Detection is evidence; the decision is the limit check.
svg.title: The aircraft inspection image: two images, one disposition
svg.text: The aircraft inspection image: two images, one disposition
Outside and inside the aircraft are different imaging problems, but both end in a limit check against the maintenance manual and a signed release.
